text:
If you are an engineering or economics student (or just very smart), you might want to consider doing a minor in mathematics. For completing the minor, you would need to complete 5 courses: 
1. MAT240 (Calculus and Analytical Geometry III), 
2. MAT370 (Real and Complex Analysis), 
3. MAT480 (Differential Equations), 
4. MAT490 (Advanced Engineering Mathematics), and 
5. MAT495 (Abstract Algebra)
The only prerequisite for each of these courses (except MAT240) is MAT250 (Calculus and Analytical Geometry IV). MAT240 is being offered in every trimester, at least for now. On the other hand, MAT370 was offered in spring, and MAT480 is currently being offered in summer. Actually, 370, 480, 490, and 495 will continue to be offered cyclically as long as there are enough interested students.
So, if you want to do a minor in math, have already completed MAT250, and won't mind studying at NSU till 192 (that's when MAT 370 would be offered again provided that there are enough interested students), you may want to take MAT480 in summer. According to the notice for phase 2 and 3 of advising, a student can take courses they did not pre-advise for in these phases. So you can take MAT 480 even if you did not pre-advise for it. See less

text:
Is the math minor worth it?
Like most of the other things in life, the math minor would be what you make out of it. Still, I would try to answer the question from 3 different angles.
Intellectual worth
-----------------------
The real purpose of university education is teaching you how to learn and think rather than quantifying your worth by a mere number between 0 and 4. The math minor courses, in particular, are there to teach you how to think in an abstract manner, how to critically examine your work, and how to read and write rigorous proofs. The training you would receive from the math minor cannot be matched by any other major/minor at NSU.
Honestly speaking, the math courses up to MAT 350 and 361 don't require much creative thought, and you can get good grades in them just by practicing the problems. In contrast, most of the math minor courses would make you think creatively. You would actually need to understand the techniques you would be taught and couple that with your own creative insights to do well. This can be challenging but the math minor is really one of those things where the fun lies in the difficulty.
I have done MAT370, MAT240, and MAT480 so far. Among them, MAT370 was very intellectually rewarding, and I would recommend it as an open elective to any student who likes to learn things just for the fun of learning. MAT240 is not even an actual math minor course and has to be taken only because it was in the required curriculum when the minor got approval from UGC. Lastly, though MAT480 is supposed to be a strong analytical course that teaches how the techniques used in solving differential equations can be proved to be correct, it was watered down to a subset of MAT350 when I took it. The reason is the majority of the students in my MAT480 were Economics students who had not done MAT350, and the instructor wanted to accommodate them. If you take MAT480 in the future, you experience may vary (I hope it does).
Academic worth
---------------------
When you would apply to foreign universities for masters or doctorate in relevant disciplines, admission committees will view your application more favorably. To quote PPD sir, "Getting a B+ in MAT370 is more valuable than getting an A any of your calculus course."
Financial worth
--------------------
There aren't many math minor graduates from NSU. I know about one math minor student who got a job at Google, and one who went on to do Ph.D. at Rice and subsequently turned down job offers from Google and Oracle to work at Two Sigma. 
In MAT370, PPD sir used to lament about how hard it is for him to find faculty for math courses and used to inspire us to do a Ph.D. in math so that he could hire us in the future. If you plan to become an academic, this is something you may want to consider.
That's my brief evaluation of the math minor. If you would like to to do the math minor as well, you would need to complete the following 5 courses:
1. MAT240 (Calculus and Analytical Geometry III), 
2. MAT370 (Real and Complex Analysis), 
3. MAT480 (Differential Equations), 
4. MAT490 (Advanced Engineering Mathematics), and 
5. MAT495 (Abstract Algebra)
The only prerequisite for each of these courses (except MAT240) is MAT250 (Calculus and Analytical Geometry IV). 
MAT370 and MAT490 would be offered in Spring 2019. If you are really interested in the minor, pre-advise for and take both of these courses. This might, in fact, be your last chance join the minor at a point from which you can actually finish it.
I would end this with an anecdote. When I was doing MAT370 under PPD sir, he used to remind us we are studying the subject of the Newton and should not expect things to be easy. So if you are the kind of person who wants to be on Newton's boat, do the math minor! See less
